translations.text: These are the names of the sons of Israel who had gone into Egypt with Jacob their father; each man went in with his whole household:
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah,
Issachar, Zebulun and Benjamin,
Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
But Joseph was already there. All the souls of Jacob numbered seventy-five.
Joseph died, and all his brothers, and that whole generation.
But the sons of Israel increased and multiplied and became teeming, and grew exceedingly strong, for that land made them multiply.
Another king arose in Egypt who did not know Joseph,
and he said to his people: Behold, this race of the sons of Israel is a great multitude, greater than ours.
Come, let us subdue them, lest they multiply, and if at any time war comes upon us, they join our enemies and fight against us, and so go out of the land.
And he set over them overseers of the work, so that they might afflict them with labour; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses, the two, which is the city of the sun.
But the more they oppressed them, the more these grew exceedingly strong, and the Egyptians loathed the sons of Israel.
By force [?].
And they made their life bitter with pain through that hard labour, with clay and brick and every kind of work in the field, every labour by which they harshly subjugated them.
The king of Egypt spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah,
and he said: When you go in to deliver the Hebrew women and they are giving birth, if it is a male, kill him, and if it is a female, let her live.
But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of the Egyptians had commanded them. [?] the midwives
and he said to them: Why have you done this thing and kept the male children alive?
The midwives said to Pharaoh: The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women, for they give birth before the midwives come in, and only then do they call us in.
And God did good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew exceedingly strong,
for the midwives feared God. They built houses for themselves.
And Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying: Every male child born to the Hebrews, throw into the river, and let every female live.
There was a certain man of the tribe of Levi who took a wife from the daughters of Levi and had her as his wife.
She conceived and bore a son. When they saw that he was handsome, they hid him for three months.
And when she could no longer hide him, his mother took a little ark, coated it with pitch, laid the child in it, and set it at the edge of the river.
And his sister watched from a distance to see what would happen to him.
Pharaoh's daughter went down to the river to bathe, and her maidservants walked here and there along the riverbank. She saw the basket among the reeds, sent a maidservant, and had it brought to her.
She opened it and saw the child crying inside the basket. Pharaoh's daughter rescued him and said, "This is one of the Hebrews' children."
The child's sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Do you want me to call a nursing woman from among the Hebrews for you, to nurse the child for you?"
Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Go and call her." So the girl went and called the child's mother.
Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Keep this child for me and nurse him, and I will give you your wages." The woman took the child
and brought him to Pharaoh's daughter. He became her son, and she named him Moses and said, "I drew him out of the water."
Many days later Moses grew up. He went out to his brothers, the sons of Israel, to see their hardship, and he saw an Egyptian man beating a Hebrew man, one of his brothers, the sons of Israel.
He looked this way and that and saw no one, so he killed the Egyptian and buried him in the sand.
He went out on the next day and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He said to the one who was harming his neighbour, "Men, you are brothers. Why are you harming one another?"
But the man said, "Who made you ruler and judge over us? Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" Moses was afraid and said, "Has this matter become known like this?"
Pharaoh heard about this and tried to kill Moses. Moses fled from Pharaoh's presence and lived as a stranger in the land of Midian, and he sat down by the well.
The priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they tended the sheep of their father Jethro. They came to draw water, and while they were filling the watering troughs to water their father's sheep,
the shepherds came and drove them away. Moses got up, rescued them, drew water for them and watered their sheep.
They went in to Jethro their father, and he said to them, "Why have you come home so quickly today?"
They said to him, "An Egyptian man rescued us from the shepherds, drew water for us and watered our sheep."
He said to his daughters, "Where is he? Why did you leave the man behind? Call him so that he may eat bread."
Moses settled with the man, and the man gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as his wife.

The woman conceived and bore a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, "For I am a stranger in a foreign land." He named the second son Eliezer, saying, "The God of my father helped me and delivered me from the hands of Pharaoh."
After many days the king of Egypt died. The sons of Israel groaned because of their harsh labours and cried out, and their cry reached God.
God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob,
and God looked upon the sons of Israel and made himself known to them.
Moses was tending the sheep of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the sheep into the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
An angel appeared to him in a flame of fire from within the bush. He saw that the bush was blazing with fire, but the bush was not burned up.
Moses said, "I will go over and see this great sight, why the bush is not burned up."
When God saw that he was coming to look, the Lord called to him from within the bush and said, "Moses, Moses!" And he said, "What is it?"
The Lord said to him, "Do not come near here. Take the sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground."
And he said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob." Moses turned his face away, for he was afraid to look before God.
The Lord said to Moses, "I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their suffering.

I have come down to rescue them from the hands of the Egyptians, to bring them out of that land, and to bring them into a very good land, a land flowing with milk and honey, the place of the Canaanites and the Hittites, the Amorites and the Hivites, the Perizzites and the Girgashites and the Jebusites.
And now the cry of the sons of Israel has reached me, and I have seen the suffering that the Egyptians inflict on them.
So now come, and I will send you to Pharaoh, the king of the Egyptians, and you shall bring my people, the sons of Israel, out of the land of Egypt."
Moses said to God, "Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, the king of the Egyptians, and bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt?"

God spoke to Moses and said, "I will be with you, and this shall be the sign for you that I have sent you: when you have brought my people out of the land of Egypt, they shall serve God in this place."
Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is his name?' What shall I tell them?"
God said to Moses, "I am who I am." And he said, "Say this to the sons of Israel: 'He who is has sent me to you.'"
God also said to Moses again, "Say this to the sons of Israel: 'The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God [?]'" [text breaks off]
[?] your hand." And he brought it out, and his hand was white as snow.
Then he said again, "Put your hand into your bosom." He put his hand back into his bosom, and when he took his hand out of his bosom, it had returned to the colour of the rest of his flesh.
"If they do not believe you or listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe you and listen to you because of the voice of the second sign.

And if they do not believe you even after these two signs and do not listen to your voice, take some water from the river and pour it on the dry ground, and the water you take from the river will become blood on the ground."

Moses said to the Lord, "I beg you, Lord, I am not capable, neither before now [literally 'since yesterday and the day before'] nor since you began to speak to your servant, for I am weak of voice and heavy of tongue."
God said to Moses: "Who gave man a mouth? Or who made the hearing and the deaf? Was it not I, the Lord God?"
"Now go, and I will open your mouth and teach you what you are to say."
And Moses said: "I beg you, Lord, seek out someone else who is able, whom you may send."

The Lord was angered with wrath against Moses and said: "Is not Aaron there, your brother the Levite? I know that he will speak for you. And behold, he is coming out to meet you, and he will see you and rejoice in his heart."
"And you shall tell him these words and put my words in his mouth, and I will open your mouth and his mouth and teach you what you are to do."
"And he will speak for you to the people; he will be a mouth for you, and you will be to him in the place of God."
"And take in your hand that rod which was turned into a serpent, with which you will perform the signs."

Moses went away from there and returned to Jethro, his father-in-law, and said to him: "Let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt and see whether they are still alive." Jethro said to Moses: "Go, go in good health!" After many days the king of the Egyptians died.
The Lord said to Moses in Midian: "Go, set out for Egypt, for all those who sought your life have died."
Moses took his wife and children, set them on beasts of burden [?], and returned to Egypt.

The Lord said to Moses: "When you go and return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the signs that I have put in your hand. But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will not let my people go."
"You shall say to Pharaoh: Thus says the Lord: Israel is my firstborn son."
"I said to you: Let my people go, so that they may serve me. If you will not let them go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son."
It happened on the way, at the lodging place, that an angel of the Lord met him and sought to kill him.
And Zipporah took a sharp stone [?] and cut off her son's foreskin, and she fell at his feet and said: "The blood of my son's circumcision has stopped."
And the angel went away from him, because she said: "The blood of my child's circumcision has stopped."
The Lord said to Aaron: "Go out and meet Moses in the wilderness." He went out and met him on the mountain of God, and they kissed each other.
And Moses told Aaron all these words of God for which he had been sent, and all the ordinances which he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron came and gathered the elders of the children of Israel.
And Aaron spoke all the words which God had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people.
The people believed and rejoiced, because the Lord had looked upon his people, the children of Israel, and because he had seen their affliction. The people bowed down and worshipped the Lord.
After this Moses and Aaron went in and said to Pharaoh: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Send out my people, so that they may serve me in the wilderness."
And Pharaoh said: "Who is he, that I should listen to him and let the children of Israel go? I do not know the Lord, nor will I let Israel go."

And they said to him: "The God of the Hebrews has summoned us. Let us go a three days' journey into the wilderness, so that we may offer sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest death or the sword befall us."
The king of the Egyptians said to them: "Moses and Aaron, why are you turning the people away from their work? Go, each of you, to your own work."
And Pharaoh said: "Look, the people of the land have now become many. Do not release them from their work any longer."
And on that day Pharaoh commanded the people's taskmasters and the scribes, and said:
"Do not give them straw for making bricks any more, as you did yesterday and the day before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.

And lay on them the same set number of bricks that they make every day; let them not reduce it at all. For they are idle, and that is why they cry out, saying, 'Let us go out and offer sacrifice to the Lord our God.'
Let the work be heavy on these men, and let them be busy with it, and not be busy with empty words."
The people's taskmasters and the scribes hurried them on and said to them: "Thus says Pharaoh: 'I will no longer give you straw.'
Go yourselves and gather straw wherever you can find it, and do not reduce your set task at all, not even by one."
And the people scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
But the taskmasters hurried them on and said to them: "Finish your set work each day, just as when you were given straw."

And the scribes from the race of the sons of Israel, whom Pharaoh's overseers had set over them, were beaten and asked: "Why have you not finished your set work of bricks today, the same as yesterday and the day before?"
The scribes of the sons of Israel went in before Pharaoh and said to him: "Why do you treat your servants like this?
You give your servants no straw, and yet you tell us to make the same number of bricks? And look, your servants are being beaten; in this way you wrong your own people."
Pharaoh said to them: "You are idle, you have time on your hands, and that is why you say, 'Let us go out and serve our God.'
Now go and work. Straw will not be given to you, but you must deliver the set number of bricks."
The scribes of the sons of Israel saw that they were in trouble, since they had been told, "You must not reduce the set daily amount."
They met Moses and Aaron, who were coming toward them, just as they were coming out from Pharaoh.
And they said to them: "May God look upon you and judge you, for you have made our fragrance loathsome before Pharaoh and before his servants, putting a sword in their hands to kill us."
Moses turned to the Lord and said: "Lord, why have you brought evil on this people, and why did you send me?
Ever since I went in to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has done evil to your people, and you have not delivered your people."
The Lord said to Moses: "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh. With a strong hand he will send them out, and with a high arm he will drive them out of his land."
God spoke to Moses and said to him: "I am the Lord,
who appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, whose God I am; but I did not make my name 'Lord' known to them.
And I established my covenant with them, to give them the land of the Canaanites, the land in which they were sojourners, in which they lived.
And I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered your covenant.

Go, speak to the children of Israel and say to them: I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from the oppression of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from their affliction, and I will set you free with a raised arm and with great judgment.
And I will take you to be my people, and I will be your God, and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the oppression of the Egyptians.
And I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out my hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; I will give it to you as an inheritance, I the Lord.
Moses spoke thus to the children of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses because of their faintness of spirit and because of their harsh labours.
The Lord said to Moses:
Go in and speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, that he may send the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
Moses spoke before God and said: Behold, the children of Israel have not listened to me; how then will Pharaoh listen to me, for I am mute?!
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them, and gave them a command concerning Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, that he should let the children of Israel go out of the land of Egypt.
And these are the heads of their fathers' houses: the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi. These are the families of Reuben.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad, Jachin and Zohar, and Shaul, who was the son of the woman of the seacoast. These are the tribes of the sons of Simeon.
And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, Kohath, Merari. And the years of the life of Levi were one hundred and thirty-seven.
And these are the sons of Gershon: Tobeli and Shimei, of their father's house.
The sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. And the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred and thirty years.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the fathers' houses of Levi, according to their generations.

And Amram took Jochebed, the daughter of his father's brother, as his own wife, and she bore him Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister. And the years of the life of Amram were one hundred and thirty-six years.
The sons of Izhar: Korah and Nepheg and Zichri.
The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, Elzaphan and Sithri.
And Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, as his wife, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
The sons of Korah: Assir, Elkanah and Abiathar. These are the offspring of Korah.
And Eleazar, the son of Aaron, took one of the daughters of Putiel as his wife, and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the tribes of Levi according to their births.
These are the Moses and Aaron to whom God spoke about bringing the children of Israel out of Egypt with all their host.
These are the ones who spoke to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and they brought the children of Israel out of Egypt; these are Aaron and Moses.
On the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt
he said: I am the Lord; speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, all that I have told you.
And Moses said before the Lord: Behold, I am weak of voice. How will Pharaoh listen to me?
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him: "See, I am making you a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.
You shall tell him everything that I command you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, so that he will send the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and I will multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and by my power I will bring my people, the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt with great vengeance.
And all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, who laid my hand upon Egypt and brought the children of Israel out from among them."
Moses and Aaron did so; as the Lord had commanded them, so they did.
Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:

"If Pharaoh speaks to you and says, 'Perform a wonder or a sign,' then say to Aaron your brother: 'Take that rod and throw it on the ground before Pharaoh and before his servants,' and it shall become a serpent."
Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and did just as the Lord had commanded them. Aaron threw down the rod before Pharaoh and his servants, and it became a serpent.
Pharaoh summoned the wise men and the sorcerers of Egypt. And the sorcerers of Egypt did the same by their sorceries:
each one threw down his rod, and they became serpents. And Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.
But Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not listen to them, as the Lord had told them.
The Lord said to Moses: "Pharaoh's heart is heavy; he refuses to let my people go.
Go to Pharaoh tomorrow. See, he is going out to the river of waters; meet him on the bank of the river. And take in your hand the rod that was turned into a serpent.
And say to him: 'The Lord God of the Hebrews has sent me to you and said: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness. And see, until now you have not listened.'
Thus says the Lord: 'By this you shall know that I am the Lord: see, I will strike the water of this river with this rod that is in my hand, and it shall be turned into blood,
and the fish of the river shall die, and the rivers shall stink, and the Egyptians shall not be able to drink.'"

The Lord said to Moses: "Say to Aaron your brother: 'Take your rod and stretch it out over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers and over the channels of their waters.' And they shall become blood, and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, in wood and in stone."

Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded them. Aaron raised his rod and struck the water of the river before Pharaoh and before his servants, and all the waters of the river were turned into blood.
The fish of the river died, and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river, and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
The sorcerers of Egypt did the same by their sorceries. And Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not let the people go, as the Lord had told him.
Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his mind even to this.
All the Egyptians dug around the river so that they might drink water, and they could not drink the water from the river.
Seven days were completed after the Lord struck the river.
The Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says the Lord: Send out my people, so that they may serve me.
If you do not wish to send them out, behold, I will strike all your borders with frogs.

The river will bring forth frogs; they will come up and go into your houses, and into the storerooms of your bedchambers, and onto your beds, and into the houses of your servants and of your people, and into your bread-store and your oven;
the frogs will come up upon you and upon your people.
The Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron your brother: Stretch out that rod with your hand over the river and over the canals and the pools, and bring up frogs.
And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt and brought up frogs. The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
The sorcerers of Egypt did the same with their sorceries and brought up frogs. The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them: Pray for me to the Lord, and take these frogs away from me and from my people, and I will let the people go, and you may serve the Lord.

Moses said to Pharaoh: Appoint for me when I shall pray for you, for your servants, and for your people, so that the frogs may vanish from you, from your people, and from your houses, and remain only in the rivers.
And he said: Tomorrow. Moses said to him: As you have said, so that you may know that there is no one besides the Lord.
And the frogs will be destroyed from you, from your houses and your courtyards, and from your servants and your people; they will remain only in the rivers.
Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. And Moses cried out to the Lord for deliverance from the frogs at the time, as Pharaoh had said.
And the Lord did so, as Moses had said. And the frogs died out from the houses, from the courtyards, and from the fields.
And they were gathered into heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
When Pharaoh saw that he had been given relief, his heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had told them.

The Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron your brother: Stretch out that rod with your hand and strike the dust of the earth. And there will be gnats upon people and upon four-footed beasts and in all the land of Egypt.
Aaron stretched out the rod with his hand and struck the dust of the earth, and there were gnats in all the land of Egypt.
The sorcerers of Egypt also did the same, trying to bring forth gnats, and they could not. And there were gnats upon people and upon four-footed beasts.
The sorcerers said to Pharaoh: This is the finger of God. Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not listen to them, as the Lord had told them.

The Lord said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, for he goes out to the river, and say to him: Thus says the Lord: Send out my people, so that they may serve me in the wilderness.

If you do not wish to send out my people so that they may serve me in the wilderness, behold, I will send dog-flies upon you, upon your servants, and upon your people, and the houses of Egypt will be filled with dog-flies, and so will the land on which they live.
And on that day I will set apart gloriously the land of Goshen, where my people live. There will be no dog-flies there, so that you may know that I am the Lord, the God of all the earth.
And I will make a distinction between my people and your people. Tomorrow there will be a sign upon the land.
And the Lord did so. He brought a multitude of dog-flies into Pharaoh's house, into the houses of his servants and into all the land of Egypt, and the land was ruined by the dog-flies.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them, "Go and serve your God here in this land."

Moses said to him, "It is not possible to do that. We may not offer the abomination of Egypt to the Lord our God. If we offer the abomination of Egypt to the Lord our God before them, they will stone us to death.
Instead, we will go a three days' journey into the wilderness and offer sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he told us."
And Pharaoh said, "I will let you go, and you may serve the Lord your God in the wilderness. But do not go far when you go out into the wilderness. Pray to the Lord for me."

Moses said, "See, I am going out from you and your servants, and I will pray to God, and the dog-flies will depart from you, from your servants and from your people. But let Pharaoh no longer deceive himself by refusing to let this people go to offer sacrifice to God."
Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.
And the Lord did as Moses had said. The dog-flies were removed from Pharaoh, from his servants and from his people, and not a single one remained.
But this time too Pharaoh hardened his heart and would not let the people go.
The Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, so that they may serve me.
If you will not let my people go, and still hold on to them,
then the hand of the Lord will fall on their livestock in the fields, on the horses and the [?], on the cattle and the sheep: a very great death.
And at that time I will make a glorious distinction between the livestock of the Egyptians and the livestock of the children of Israel. Not one of the animals of the children of Israel will die."
And God set this appointed time, saying, "Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land."
And all the livestock of Egypt died, but not one of the animals of the children of Israel died.
Pharaoh saw that not one of the animals of the children of Israel had died. Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not let the people go.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said, "Take handfuls of ash from the furnace, and let Moses throw it into the air toward heaven before Pharaoh and before his servants.

And let it become dust over all the land of Egypt. On people and on all four-footed animals there will be boils breaking out in blisters. It will break out on people and animals throughout all the land of Egypt."
Moses took the dust from the furnace before Pharaoh and threw it into the air toward heaven. And boils broke out in blisters on people and on four-footed animals.
And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the plague, for the boils were on the magicians too, and on all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh hardened his heart and did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
The Lord said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness.
If not, now at this very time I will send all my plagues into your heart, and on your servants and your people, and you will know that there is no other besides me in all the earth.
For now I will stretch out my hand and strike you and your people, and you will be wiped off the earth.
For this very reason I have kept you, so that I may show my power in you, and so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
For you still hold back my people and do not let them go.
Behold, tomorrow at this very hour I will rain down a very great hail, such as has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now.
Now hurry to gather your livestock and all that you have in the field. Every man and beast that is found in the field and does not go into a house, the hail will fall on it and it will die.
Those of Pharaoh's servants who feared the word of the Lord gathered their livestock into the houses.
But those who did not heed the word of the Lord in their minds left them out in the field.
The Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be hail in all the land of Egypt, on men and on livestock and on all the green plants of the field.
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and fire flashed down, and the Lord rained hail on all the land of Egypt, from man to beast.
There was hail, and burning fire mixed with the hail. And the hail was very great, such as had not been in all the land of Egypt since a nation had been upon it.
And the hail struck down throughout all the land of Egypt, from man to beast, and every green plant. Whatever was in the field the hail struck down, and it struck down every tree of the field.
But in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, there was no hail.
Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them: I have sinned now against the Lord. The Lord is righteous, and I and my people are ungodly.
Pray for me to the Lord, and let these voices of God cease from now on, this fire and hail, and I will let you go.

Moses said to him: As soon as I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands to the Lord, and these voices will cease, and there will be no more hail or rain, so that you may know that this land is the Lord's.
But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear God.
The flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was in seed.
But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they were late [?].
Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh and spread out his hands to the Lord. The thunder ceased, and the hail and rain no longer poured down on the earth.
When Pharaoh saw that the thunder, the hail, and the rain had ceased, he went on sinning still more, and hardened his heart and the hearts of his servants.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not let the people, the children of Israel, go, just as the Lord had told Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said: Go in to Pharaoh, for I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants, so that these signs may come upon them one after another [?],
so that you may tell in the ears of your children and of your children's children how greatly I mocked those Egyptians, and of my signs which I performed among them, and you shall know that I am [?].
Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him: "Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews: Will you not humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that they may serve me.
If you will not let my people go, behold, tomorrow at this very hour I will send [?] locusts, very great in number, into all your borders.

And they shall cover the face of the earth, and you will not be able to see the earth; and they shall eat all that is left of the land, which was left to you from the hail, and they shall eat every tree and plant of yours on the earth.

And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your servants, and all the houses, as many as there are in the land of Egypt, such as your fathers have never seen, nor their fathers before them, from the time they were on the earth until this present day." And Moses turned and went out from Pharaoh.
Pharaoh's servants said to Pharaoh: "How long shall this torment be upon us? Let these men go, so that they may serve the Lord their God. Or do you not know that Egypt has perished?"
They brought Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh. Pharaoh said to them: "Go and serve the Lord your God. But who exactly are those who will go?"
Moses said to him: "We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and daughters, with our flocks and cattle, for it is a feast of the Lord our God."
Pharaoh said to them: "Let it be so! The Lord be with you! For I will let you go — and perhaps your belongings too? See, evil lies before you.
Not so; but let the men go and serve God, for that is what you are seeking." And they drove them out from Pharaoh's presence.

The Lord said to Moses: "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let locusts come up upon the land and eat the green plants of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail has left."
And Moses raised the rod toward heaven, and the Lord brought a wind from the south upon the land all day — all that day and all night. And when morning came, the south wind brought up the locusts
and spread them over all the land of Egypt. And they settled on all the borders of Egypt in very great numbers; before them there had been no such locusts, nor after them was there ever the like.

And they covered the face of the earth and devoured all the green plants of the land and the fruit of the trees that had remained from the hail. Nothing green remained on any of the trees or in all the green plants of the land throughout all Egypt.
Pharaoh hastened to summon Moses and Aaron and said to them: "I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you.
Now bear this sin only this once, and pray for me to the Lord your God, and take this death away from me."
Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.
And the Lord sent a fierce wind from the sea. It took up the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea, and not one locust remained in all the land of Egypt.
And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
The Lord said to Moses: "Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt, a darkness that can be felt with the hand."
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was darkness, thick darkness, mist and fog over all the land of Egypt for three days.
And no one rose from his bed for three days; but for all the children of Israel there was light everywhere they went.
Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them: "Go out and serve the Lord your God, but leave your sheep and cattle behind. Take your goods with you as well."
Moses said: "No, you too must give us something for sacrifice and offering, and we will offer it to the Lord our God.

Our flocks too shall go out with us, and we will not leave behind even one hoof of them, for we will take some of them for the service of the Lord our God. For we do not know what we shall offer to the Lord our God until we get there."
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let them go.
And Pharaoh said to Moses: "Get away from me, and take care not to see my face again. On the day you appear before me, you shall die."
Moses said: "I will not appear before your face again."
The Lord said to Moses: "I will bring one more plague upon Pharaoh and upon all Egypt, and after that he will let you go from here. And when he lets you go, he will drive you out completely.
Speak privately into the ears of the people, and let each man ask of his neighbour, and each woman of her neighbour, vessels of gold and of silver, and clothing."

And the Lord gave his people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them. And the man Moses became very great in the sight of the Egyptians, and in the sight of Pharaoh and of his servants.
Moses said: "Thus says the Lord: About midnight I will go into the midst of Egypt.

And every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sits on the throne, to the firstborn of the maidservant who sits at the mill, and to the firstborn of all the cattle.
And there shall be an outcry in all the land of Egypt such as there will never be again.

But among all the children of Israel no dog shall move its tongue, against man or beast, so that you may know how greatly the Lord will make a distinction between the Egyptians and the children of Israel.

And all these servants of yours will come to me and bow down to me, saying: 'Go out, you and all your people of whom you speak.' And after that you will go out." And Moses went out from Pharaoh's presence in anger.
The Lord said to Moses: "Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that I may multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt."

Moses and Aaron did all these things in the land of Egypt before Pharaoh, and the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not listen to the children of Israel and let them go out of the land of Egypt.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, and said to them:
"This month shall be for you the beginning of months; it shall be the first for you among the months of the year.
Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel and say: On the tenth day of this month each man shall take a lamb, one for each household of their families, each one a lamb for a household.

If there are too few in the household to eat the lamb, let him join with him his neighbour and companion according to the number of persons. Each of you shall count how many there will be for that lamb.
Your lamb shall be without blemish, a year-old male. You shall take it from the lambs or from the kids.
And it shall be kept by you until the fifteenth day of this month, and the whole multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
And they shall take some of its blood and smear it on both doorposts and on the lintel of the door in the house where they eat it.
And they shall eat the flesh roasted with fire, and they shall eat unleavened bread with bitter wild herbs.
You shall not eat any of it raw, nor boiled in water, but roasted with fire, the head with the feet and the entrails.
You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it; and whatever of it remains until morning, burn with fire.
And this is how you shall eat it: with your loins girded and your sandals on your feet, and you shall eat it in haste, for it is the Passover of the Lord.
And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night and will destroy every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast, and on all the gods of Egypt I will execute vengeance, I the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are: there I will see the blood and will protect you, and the destroying plague shall not be upon you when I strike the land of Egypt.
And this day shall be a memorial for you, and you shall celebrate it as a feast

Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and from the very first day you shall remove leaven from your houses. Whoever eats leaven, that soul shall be cut off from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
And the first day shall be called holy, and the seventh day shall be called holy for you. You shall do no servile work on that day, except what is done for every soul; this alone you shall do.
And keep this commandment, for on this day I will bring your host out of the land of Egypt; and you shall observe that day throughout your generations as an everlasting ordinance.
At the beginning, on the fourteenth day of the first month, from evening you shall eat unleavened bread until the twenty-first day of the month, until evening.

For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened, that soul shall be blotted out from the congregation of Israel, from the tillers of the land to the rulers of the land.
You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.
Moses called all the elders of the sons of Israel and said to them: Go and take for yourselves a lamb according to your families, and slaughter the Passover.

And take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood, and smear some of the blood that is at the door on the front of the door, on the lintel and on both doorposts; and none of you shall go out of the doors of his house until morning.

And the Lord will come down to destroy the Egyptians and will see the blood on the lintels and the doorposts, and the Lord will pass over that door and will not let the destroyer enter your house to destroy.
Keep this word as an everlasting ordinance, and for your children forever.
When you enter the land which the Lord God has given you, as he told you, you shall keep this service.
And when your children say to you, 'What is this service?'
you shall say to them: 'This is the sacrifice of the Lord, who protected the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when he was destroying Egypt, but delivered our houses.'
The people bowed down and worshipped the Lord. Then the sons of Israel went and did as Moses and Aaron had commanded them; that is what they did.

And at midnight the Lord struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on the throne, to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and to the firstborn of all the cattle.
Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry throughout Egypt, for there was no house in which there was not someone dead.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron in the night and said to them: "Rise up and go out from among my people, you and the sons of Israel, and serve the Lord your God, as you say.
Drive out your sheep and your cattle and go, as you have said. But bless me too."
The Egyptians pressed the sons of Israel to leave the land of Egypt quickly, for they said: "We are all dying."
The people took up their dough before their [?] had been leavened, bound up in their garments, and carried it on their backs.
The sons of Israel did as Moses had ordered them. They asked for vessels of gold and silver, and for clothing.
And the Lord gave his people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent things to them. So they plundered the Egyptians.
The sons of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, six hundred thousand men on foot, besides their baggage.
A great crowd of foreigners also went up with them, along with sheep and cattle and a very large amount of livestock.

They made the dough they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened ash-cakes, for it had not leavened, because the Egyptians had driven them out and could not bear to wait; and they had not made any food ready for the journey.
The time the sons of Israel spent as foreigners, the time that they and their fathers lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, was four hundred and thirty years.
And at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, all the people of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt.
This bringing of them out of the land of Egypt is the first [?]watch. That night is the first vigil of the Lord, and it shall be kept by all the sons of Israel and by their descendants.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said: "This shall be the law of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it.
Every slave belonging to anyone, bought with silver, you shall circumcise, and then he may eat of it.
A foreigner and a hired servant shall not eat of it.
You shall eat it in a single house. You shall not leave any of its meat until morning, you shall not take any of its meat outside, and you shall not break any of its bones.
The whole congregation of the sons of Israel shall do this.

If a foreigner comes to you to keep this Passover of the Lord, you shall circumcise every male of his household. Only then may he come, and he shall be like a native of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
There shall be one law for the native and for the foreigner who has come to live among you."
And the sons of Israel did as the Lord had ordered and commanded Moses and Aaron concerning them; that is what they did.
And on that same day he brought the sons of Israel out of Egypt with their host.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
"Consecrate to me every firstborn, the first-born that opens any womb, every first one among the sons of Israel, from man to beast: it is mine."

Moses said to the people: Remember this day, on which you came out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, for the Lord brought you out from there with a strong hand. So you shall not eat leavened bread.
For today you are going out, in the new month.

And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites and the Hivites, the Girgashites and the Amorites, the Perizzites and the Jebusites, the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall perform this service in this month.
Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and the seventh day is a feast of the Lord.
You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days; you shall not see anything leavened. Nor shall there be any leaven in all your borders.
You shall tell your son on that day and say to him: This is why the Lord my God acted for me, when I was coming out of the land of Egypt.
And it shall be a sign on your hand and a memorial before your eyes, so that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth; for with a strong hand the Lord your God brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep the law year by year at its proper time, from day to day.
And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, as he swore to your fathers, and gives it to you,

that you shall set apart everything that first opens the womb, the males, for the Lord, from your cattle [?] or from all your livestock, however many you have; every male you shall consecrate to the Lord.
But the male you shall exchange for a sheep. If you do not exchange it, you shall redeem it. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem.
If your son asks you afterward and says to you, 'What is this?', you shall say to him: With a strong hand the Lord brought us out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;

when Pharaoh hardened himself against sending us away, he slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of men to the firstborn of beasts. For this reason I sacrifice to the Lord every male that opens the womb, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.
And it shall be a sign on your hand and fixed immovably before your eyes, for with a strong hand he brought you out of the land of Egypt.

And when the Lord brought out his people, the Lord did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, though it was near, for God said: Lest perhaps this people repent when they see war, and turn back to Egypt.
And the Lord led his people around by the way of the wilderness to the Red Sea. In the fifth generation the sons of Israel came out of the land of Egypt.
Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying: The Lord will surely visit you; carry my bones away with you.
And the sons of Israel set out from Succoth and encamped at Etham, beside the wilderness.
And God went before them: by day he showed them the way with a pillar of cloud, and by night with a pillar of fire.
The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not fail them before all the people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: Let them turn and encamp before the ravine, between Migdol and the sea, opposite Baal-zephon; you shall encamp before it, beside the sea.
And Pharaoh will say to his people: The sons of Israel are wandering astray in the land, for they are shut in by the wilderness.

The Lord said: I will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and he will pursue after them. And I will be glorified over Pharaoh and over all his people, and the Egyptians will understand that I am God. And they did so.

They told the king of Egypt that the people had fled. And the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they said: What is this that we have done, letting the sons of Israel go, so that they will not serve us?
Pharaoh harnessed his chariots and took all his people with him.
He took six hundred of his chosen chariots and all the horses of Egypt, and captains over them all.
And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, and of his servants, and he pursued after the sons of Israel. But the sons of Israel were going out with a strong hand.
And the Egyptians pursued after them and found them encamped by the sea: all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and the horsemen, and all his people, beyond the ravine, opposite Baal-zephon.
And Pharaoh was drawing near. The sons of Israel lifted up their eyes and saw the Egyptians [?] drawn up behind them. And they were very afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord.
And they said to Moses: Were there no graves in Egypt, that you have brought us out to die in the wilderness? What is this that you have done to us, bringing us out of Egypt?
Or is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, when we said: Let us alone, and let us serve [?]
[?] it as food, two portions, a double measure for each one. And all the rulers of the congregation came in and told Moses.

But Moses said to them: This is the word which the Lord spoke: Tomorrow is a sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord. Whatever you will bake, bake, and whatever you will boil, boil; and lay up all that is left over in your stores until morning.
And they laid some of it up until the next day, as Moses had commanded them. And it did not stink, nor did worms get into it.
Moses said to them: Eat it today, for it is the sabbath of the Lord; you will not find it in the field.
Six days you shall gather, and the seventh day is a sabbath; there will be none on that day.
On that seventh day some of the people went out to gather, and they found nothing.
The Lord said to Moses: How long will they refuse to hear my commandments and my law?
See, the Lord has given you this day, the sabbath. Therefore he himself gives you on this day bread for two days. Stay, each one of you, in your houses; let no one go out on that seventh day.
And the people kept the sabbath on the seventh day.
And the sons of Israel called its name manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like honey.

Moses said: This is the word that the Lord commanded: Fill a measure with manna, to be stored and kept for your generations, so that they may know the bread which you ate in the wilderness when the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Moses said to Aaron: Take one golden jar and put a full measure of manna in it, and set it before the Lord, to be kept for your generations,
as the Lord had commanded Moses. And Aaron set it before the Lord as a testimony and to be kept.
And the sons of Israel ate the manna for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate the manna until they came to the land of [?].
And the measure was the tenth part of the three-measure.

And the whole congregation of the sons of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin, camp by camp, each of them, by the word of the Lord, and they encamped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
And they reviled Moses and said to him: "Give us water, so that we may drink." Moses said to them: "Why do you revile me, or why do you test the Lord?"
The people thirsted for water, and there the people grumbled against Moses and said: "Why have you brought us out of Egypt to kill us and our children with thirst?"
Moses cried out to the Lord and said: "What shall I do with this people? A little more and they will stone me."
The Lord said to Moses: "Go on ahead of this people, and take with you some of the elders, and take in your hand the rod with which you struck the river, and go.
And I will stand there before you arrive, on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock and bring water out of it, and my people shall drink." And Moses did so before the sons of Israel.
And he named that place Testing and Reviling, because of the reviling by the sons of Israel and because of their testing, for they said: "Is the Lord among us or not?"
Amalek came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua: "Choose mighty men for yourself, go out, and fight Amalek tomorrow, and I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in my hand."
And Joshua did so, as Moses told him. Moses [the name is written twice in the text], Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
And whenever Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed, and whenever he lowered his hands, Amalek prevailed.

Because Moses' hands grew heavy, they brought a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. And Aaron and Hur held up Moses' hands, one on one side and one on the other. And Moses' hands stayed raised until the sun went down.
And Joshua routed Amalek and killed all his people with the edge of the sword.
The Lord said to Moses: "Write this in a book as a memorial and put it in the ears of Joshua, for I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven."
And he built an altar of the Lord there and named it: "The Lord is my refuge."
For with a hidden hand the Lord wages war against Amalek from generation to generation.
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, heard all that the Lord had done for Israel, his own people: that the Lord had brought the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought Zipporah, Moses' wife, after she had been sent away,
and his two sons. The name of one was Gershom, for he said: "I am a sojourner in a foreign land."
And the name of the second was Eliezer, for he said: "The God of my father is my helper, and he delivered me from the hand of Pharaoh."
Jethro, his father-in-law, came to Moses with his sons and his wife into the wilderness, where he was encamped at Mount Sinai.
They told Moses and said to him: "Look, Jethro, your father-in-law, is coming to you, and your wife and your two sons are with him."
And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed down to him and kissed him, and they asked after each other's welfare, and he brought them into his tent.

And Moses told his father-in-law everything the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel's sake, and all the hardship that had come upon them on the way, and how the Lord had delivered them from the hand of Pharaoh and from the hands of the Egyptians.
And Jethro was amazed at all the good things the Lord had done for them.
And Jethro said: "Blessed is the Lord, who has saved you from the hands of the Egyptians and from the hands of Pharaoh.
Now I have recognized the power, that the Lord is great, greater than all gods, because of this, that they had hoped in him."
And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took sacrifices and an offering and offered them to God. Aaron also came, and the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God.
And on the next day Moses sat down to judge the people, and all the people stood before Moses from dawn until evening.

Jethro saw everything that he was doing for the people, and he said to him: "What is this that you are doing for this people? Why do you sit alone, and all this people stands before you from morning until evening?"
And Moses said to his father-in-law: "Because this people comes to me to seek judgment from God.
Whenever there is a dispute among them, they come to me, and I judge each person, and I teach them the commandments of God and his law."
Moses' father-in-law said to him: "You are not doing this thing rightly.
You will surely wear yourself out with this unbearable [burden], both you and this people who are with you. This matter is too heavy for you; you are not able to do it alone.
Now I will advise you; listen to me, and God will be with you. Be for this people before God, and bring their words to God.
And you shall declare to them the commandments of God and his law, and you shall show them the way in which they should walk and the deeds that they should do.

And you yourself shall choose men out of all the people, capable men who serve God, righteous men who hate arrogance, and set them over them as captains of thousands, captains of hundreds, captains of fifties and captains of tens, and as scribes who bring in the people,
and let them judge this people at all times; and let them bring every heavy matter to you, but let them judge the easy matters themselves, and so they will lighten your burden and help you.
If you do this thing, your God will help you, and you will be able to lead, and all this people will go in peace to their own place."
And Moses obeyed the voice of his father-in-law and did everything just as he had told him.
And he set them over them as captains of thousands, captains of hundreds, captains of fifties and captains of tens, and as scribes who bring in and bring out,
and they judged the people at all times. But the difficult matter they brought to Moses, and every easy matter they judged themselves.
And Moses sent his father-in-law off, and he went away to his own land.
In the third month after the children of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in that month they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
And they set out from Rephidim and came into the wilderness of Sinai, and the Israelites camped there before the mountain.
And Moses went up to the mountain of God. And God called to him from the mountain and said: "Say this to the house of Jacob and tell the children of Israel:
'You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I took you up as on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.'
And now, if you will indeed listen to my voice and keep my law, you shall be my own people, acquired out of all the nations, for all the earth is mine.
You shall be to me a royal priesthood and a holy nation. Speak these words to the sons of Israel.
Moses came and called the elders of the people, and told them all these words that God had commanded him.
All the people answered together and said: "Everything that God has said we will do and obey." And Moses brought the people's words before God.
The Lord said to Moses: "Behold, I will come to you in a pillar of cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak to you, and may believe you forever." Moses told the people's words to God.
The Lord said to Moses: "Go down and charge the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their clothes.
And let them be ready by the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down upon Mount Sinai before all the people.
And set bounds for the people all around, and say to them: 'Take heed to yourselves, and do not go up the mountain or touch any part of it. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.'

No one shall lay a hand on it, for he will be stoned with stones or shot down with arrows; whether beast or man, he shall not live. When the voices and the trumpet and the cloud have departed from the mountain, then they may come up the mountain."
Moses came down from the mountain to the people and spoke to them in this way and sanctified them, and they washed their clothes.
And he said to the people: "Do not touch your wives, and be ready for three days."
And after three days, just at dawn, there were thunders and lightnings and a dark cloud on Mount Sinai. The sound of the trumpet blared loudly, and all the people in the camp trembled.
And Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of Mount Sinai.
And Mount Sinai was smoking all over, because God had come down upon it in fire, and the smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace. And the people were greatly terrified.
And the sounds of the trumpet, as they went on one after another, grew very great. Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice.
And the Lord had come down upon Mount Sinai, on the summit of the mountain, and Moses went up there.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said: "Go down and charge the people, lest they come near to God to gaze, and many of them fall.
And let the priests who draw near to God be holy, lest the Lord destroy some of them."
Moses said to God: "The people cannot approach Mount Sinai, for you charged us and told us to keep away from this mountain and to be holy."
The Lord said to him: "Go, go down, and bring Aaron up with you; but let the other priests not venture to come up to God, lest the Lord destroy some of them."
Moses went down to the people and told them this.
And the Lord spoke all these words and said:
"I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of affliction.
You shall have no foreign gods besides me.
You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor any likeness of anything that is in heaven, or that is on the earth, or that is in the waters under the earth.
You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, who repays the sin of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
and I show mercy to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not hold guiltless whoever takes the name of the Lord in vain.
Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.
Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord your God, and on it you shall do no work: you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the stranger who lives among you.
For in six days God made the heaven and the earth, the sea, and everything that is in them, and he rested on the seventh day. Therefore God blessed the seventh day and made it holy.
Honor your father and your mother, so that it may go well with you and you may live long in the good land that the Lord God will give you.
You shall not kill.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor's wife, or his field, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or any of his livestock, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
And all the people saw the sound of the trumpet and the smoking [?]. All the people were afraid and stood far off.
And they said to Moses: "You speak to us, and do not let God speak to us, lest we die."
Moses said to them: "Do not be afraid, for God has come to you to test you, so that the fear of him may be among you and so that you may not sin."
And the people stood far off, but Moses went into the thick darkness where God was.
The Lord said to Moses: "Say this to the house of Jacob and tell the children of Israel: You have seen that I spoke to you from heaven.
You shall not make for yourselves idols of gold and silver.
You shall build me an altar of earth, and on it you shall offer your sacrifices for your salvation, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I set my name, I will come and bless you.
If you build me an altar of stones, you shall not build it of hewn stone, for if you have put your hand to it, it is defiled.
You shall not go up by steps to my altar, so that your nakedness may not be exposed on it."
And these are the ordinances that he set before them:
If you acquire a Hebrew slave, he shall serve you six years, but in the seventh year he shall go out from you free, without payment [?].
If he came in alone, he shall go out alone. If his wife came in with him, his wife shall go out with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and the children shall belong to her master, and he shall go out alone.
And if that slave says, "I love my master and the children; I will not go out free,"

his master shall bring him before the judgment of God. Then he shall take him and bring him to the door, to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.
If anyone sells his daughter as a slave, she shall not go out as they go out
If she does not please her master, who had pledged her to himself, he shall let her be redeemed. But he has no right to sell her to a foreign people, because he has treated her with contempt.
If he pledges her to his son, he shall treat her according to the right of daughters.
If he takes another wife for himself, he shall not reduce her food, her clothing, or what he promised her.
If he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out free, without silver.
If anyone strikes a person and that person dies, he shall surely be put to death.
If it was not intentional, but the Lord gave him into his hands, I will give you a place where the killer may flee.
If anyone lies in wait for his neighbour with treachery and kills him, and flees there, take him down from my altar and put him to death.
Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
Whoever speaks evil of his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
If anyone steals a child of the sons of Israel and overpowers him, and he goes out [?], and the child is found with him, he shall surely be put to death.
If two men quarrel and one strikes the other with his fist or with a stone, and the man does not die but is confined to his bed,
and then gets up and walks about outside with a staff, the one who struck him shall be free of guilt. But he shall pay him for his lost time and for the cost of his healing.
If anyone strikes his male slave or his female slave with a rod and the slave dies under his hand, the slave shall surely be avenged on him.
But if the slave survives for one day or two days, he shall not be avenged, for the slave is his master's property, bought with his silver.

If two men are fighting and strike a pregnant woman, and her child miscarries while not yet formed, he shall surely be fined. Whatever the woman's husband imposes on him, he shall pay by entreaty [?].
If the child was formed, he shall give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
If anyone strikes the eye of his male slave or the eye of his female slave and destroys it, he shall let them go free in exchange for their eye.
If anyone strikes out the tooth of his male slave or the tooth of his female slave and knocks it out, he shall let them go free in exchange for their tooth.
If a bull gores a man or a woman and the person dies, the bull shall be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten, but its owner shall be free of guilt.

If the bull has been a gorer since yesterday and the day before, and its owner has been warned about it, and he has not removed it from among them, and it kills a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall die with it.
If a ransom is laid on him, he shall give as ransom whatever they lay on him, in exchange for his life, for the one whom it killed.
If it gores a son or a daughter, they shall judge him in the same way.
If the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty silver staters to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.
If someone opens a pit, or digs out a pit, and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit shall pay silver to their owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
If someone's bull gores his neighbour's bull and kills it, they shall sell the living bull and divide the silver, and they shall also divide the dead bull.

If it was known that the bull had been a gorer since the day before and yesterday, and its owner had been warned, and he did not destroy his bull, he shall give bull for bull, and the dead one shall be his.
If someone steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall give five oxen for one ox and four sheep for one sheep.
If the thief is caught breaking through a wall, and someone strikes him and he dies, it is not murder for that person.
If the sun had risen on him and he kills him, he is liable to death. If the thief has nothing to pay with, he shall be sold for what he stole.
If they catch him and the stolen animal is found alive in his possession, whether a donkey or a sheep, he shall pay back double.

If someone lets his livestock loose and they graze off a field or a vineyard, someone else's field, he shall pay the owner from his own field according to its yield. If they graze off the whole field, he shall give him the best of his fields or the best of his vineyards.
If a fire breaks out and catches in thorns and burns up a threshing floor, or a field of grain ready for harvest, or a meadow, the one who started the fire shall pay compensation.
If someone gives his neighbour silver or vessels to keep for him, and someone steals them from that man's house, then if the thief is found, he shall repay double.

If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall come forward, and the case of both parties shall be brought before God, to determine whether he has done any wrong with all that his neighbour deposited with him,

in every false claim, about an ox or a beast of burden, a sheep or a garment, or anything lost that someone is accused of, whatever it may be. The case of both parties shall be brought before God, and the one whom God finds guilty shall pay double to his neighbour.
If someone gives his neighbour a beast of burden, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to keep, and it is injured, or dies, or is carried off by raiders, and no one knows about it,

an oath before God shall be taken between the two of them that he did no wrong with all that his neighbour deposited with him. The owner of the deposit shall accept this, and he shall not demand any payment from him.
If someone steals it from him, he shall pay the owner of the deposit.
If it is torn apart by wild beasts, they shall bring him to the remains of what was eaten, and he shall not have to pay.
If anyone borrows an animal from his neighbour, and it is injured, or dies, or is carried off as plunder, and its owner is not with it, he shall make restitution.
If the owner is with it, he shall not [repay]. If it was hired for a fee, that shall be his in place of his fee.
If anyone seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, he shall take her as his own wife.
If it does not please her father, and he refuses to give her to him as a wife, the man shall give silver to the girl's father, as much as is paid for virgins.
Do not [?] sorcerers.
Everyone who lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to an idol shall surely be put to death; sacrifice only to the one God.
Do no harm to a stranger, and do not oppress strangers, for you too were strangers in the land of Egypt.
Do no harm to any widow or orphan.
If you do them harm, and they cry out and call to me, I will surely hear their voice,
and I will be enraged with anger and will destroy you with the sword, and your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend silver to your poor [?] brother who lives among you, do not press him for quick repayment, and do not charge him interest.
If you take your neighbour's garment as a pledge, give it back to him at sunset,
for that alone is his clothing and the covering for his nakedness. What will he sleep in? If he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am merciful.
Do not speak evil of God, and do not speak evil of the ruler of your people.
Do not hold back the firstfruits of your threshing floor and your winepress. Give me the firstborn of your sons.
Do the same with your ox, your sheep and your donkey: it shall stay with its mother for seven days, and on the eighth day give it to me.
And you shall be holy men. Do not eat the meat of an animal torn by wild beasts; throw it to the dogs.
Do not accept an empty report, and do not agree with a liar to act as a false witness.
Do not join the many in doing evil. Do not side with the majority of the assembly in turning aside to pervert justice.
And do not show favour to the poor in a court case.
If you come across your enemy's ox or donkey that has strayed, bring it back and give it to its owner.
If you see your enemy's donkey fallen down under its load, do not pass it by, but lift it up together with him.
Do not pervert justice for the poor in their court case.
Keep away from every evil word. Do not kill the innocent and the righteous, and do not acquit the ungodly for a bribe.
And you shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of those who see and perverts righteous words.
And you shall not oppress the stranger, for you know the soul of the stranger, for you too were strangers in the land of Egypt.
For six years you shall sow your land and gather in its produce,

but in the seventh year you shall make a release: you shall leave it alone, and the poor of your people shall eat, and what is left of it shall be for the wild beasts of the field. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your fig orchard.
For six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day your ox and the stranger shall rest.
Keep everything that I have told you. Do not call to mind the name of foreign gods, and do not let it be heard from your mouth.
Three times in the year you shall hold a feast for me.

Take care to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread: for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at that time [?] of the month of new grain, for in that month you came out of the land of Egypt. You shall not appear before my face empty-handed.
You shall keep the Feast of Harvest, of the firstfruits of your labours, of whatever you sow in your land, and the Feast of Completion at the going out of the year, when you gather in your produce.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God.
When I drive out the nations from before you and enlarge your borders, you shall not offer the blood of my sacrifices with leavened bread, and the fat of my feasts shall not remain until morning.
The first of your firstfruits you shall bring into the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother's milk.
And behold, I will send my angel before you, to guard you on the way and to bring you into the land which I swore to you.
Take heed to yourself and listen to him, and do not disobey him. For he will not pardon you, because my name is upon him.

If you truly listen to my words and do everything that I have commanded you, and keep my covenant, you shall be my treasured people above all nations, for all the earth is mine; and you shall be to me a royal, priestly people, a holy nation. Speak these words to the children of Israel: If you truly listen to my words and do everything that I tell you, I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
For my angel shall go as a guide for you and bring you in to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Girgashite and the Jebusite, and I will destroy them.
You shall not bow down to their gods nor serve them. You shall not act according to their deeds, but you shall utterly tear down and utterly smash their sacred pillars.
And you shall serve the Lord your God. And I will bless your bread and your wine and your water, and I will turn sickness away from you.
There shall be no one childless or barren in your land. I will fill up the number of your days,
and I will send fear and trembling ahead of you as a guide, and I will throw into confusion all the nations among whom you enter there, and I will make all your enemies flee before you.
And I will send the hornet ahead of you, and they shall drive out the Amorites and the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites from before you.
I will not drive them out in a single year, so that the land does not become desolate and the wild beasts of the earth do not multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you increase and inherit the land.

And I will set your borders from the Red Sea as far as the Philistines, and from the desert as far as the great river Euphrates; and I will give the inhabitants of that land into your hands, and I will drive them out from before you, until you increase and inherit the land.
You shall not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
And they shall not dwell in your land, so that they do not make you sin against me. If you serve their gods, they will be a stumbling block to you.
And to Moses he said: Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron and Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and worship the Lord from afar.
And Moses alone shall come near to God, but they shall not come near, and the people shall not come up with them.
Moses went in and told the people all the words of God and his ordinances. The people answered with a loud voice and said: All the words that the Lord has spoken we will do and we will obey.
And Moses wrote down all these words of the Lord. Moses rose early in the morning and built an altar below the mountain with twelve stones, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
And Moses sent the young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered sacrifices, and young bulls as an offering of salvation to God.
And Moses took half of the blood and poured it into a bowl, and the other half of the blood he sprinkled around the altar, at a distance [?].
And he took the book of the law and read it aloud in the hearing of the people, and they said: Everything that the Lord has said we will do and we will obey.
Moses took the blood, sprinkled it on the people, and said: This is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made concerning all these words.
And Moses went up, with Aaron and Nadab and Abihu and seventy of the elders of Israel,
and they saw the place where the God of Israel stood, and under his feet there was something like a work of brick, of carbuncle and sapphire, like the firmament of heaven in its purity.
And of the chosen ones of Israel not one died; and they saw the place of God, and they ate and drank.
And the Lord said to Moses: Come up to me on the mountain and stay there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, the law and my commandments, which I have written to give them as law.
Moses arose, with Joshua who attended him, and they went up the mountain of God.
And to the elders he said: Wait there quietly until I come back to you. Look, Aaron and Hur are with you. If anyone has a case to be judged, let him go to them.
And Moses and Joshua went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
And on the seventh day the Lord called Moses from out of the cloud.
And the sight of the glory of God was like a fire blazing on the summit of the mountain in front of the sons of Israel.
And Moses went into the midst of the cloud and went up the mountain, and he was there on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: Bring offerings from everyone whose heart is willing; bring me firstfruits as an offering to me.
