And this is the offering that you shall take from them:
Gold and silver and bronze, blue and scarlet and double purple, and spun [?] fine linen, and goats' hair;
and rams' skins dyed red [?], and blue [?] skins, and wood that does not rot;
and sardius stone and carbuncles for carving, for the shoulder-pieces and for the [?].
And make me a sanctuary, and I will appear to you.
And make it for me in every way according to what I show you on the mountain, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its vessels; that is how you shall make it.
And make an ark of the testimony out of wood that does not rot: its length two and a half cubits, its width one and a half cubits, and its height one and a half cubits.
And overlay it with pure gold; overlay it inside and outside. And make for it a wreathed rim of gold all around.
And make for it four rings of gold and fasten them at its four corners: two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
And make carrying poles of wood that does not rot, and overlay them with gold.
And put the carrying poles through the rings that are at the sides of the ark, so that the ark may be carried by them.
And the carrying poles shall stay in the rings of the ark of the law, never to be moved.
And put the testimonies that I will give you inside the ark.
And make the mercy seat of pure gold, to be set upon it, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
And make two cherubim of carved gold, and set them at the two ends of the mercy seat.
Make one at one end and the other cherub at the other end of the mercy seat; make these two cherubim so that they are at its two ends.
And both shall spread their wings upward, and they shall cover the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall be turned toward each other and toward the mercy seat.
And put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and inside the ark put the testimonies that I will give you.

And I will appear to you from there, and I will speak to you from above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the testimony, about everything that I command you for the children of Israel.
And make a table of gold: its length two cubits, its width one cubit, and its height one and a half cubits.
And make for it wreathed rims of gold all around. And make for it a crown a span wide all around.
And make four rings of gold and fasten them at the four corners of its legs,
beneath the crown.

And the rings shall hold the carrying poles, so that the table may be carried by them. And make the carrying poles of wood that does not rot, and overlay them with pure gold, and the table shall be carried by them.
And make its dishes and [?] (bowls?), cups and ladles, with which you will make offerings; make them of pure gold.
And on the table, before me, set the perpetual bread, always before me.
And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold; you shall make the lampstand of hammered work. Its shaft, its branches, its cups, its knobs and its lilies shall be of one piece with it.
Six branches shall come out on one side: three branches of the lampstand on one side, and three branches of the lampstand on the other side.
And the cups shall be shaped like nuts, on each branch, with its knobs and its lilies.
A knob beneath two of the branches, of one piece with it, and a knob beneath the four branches, of one piece with it. So it shall be for the six branches of the lampstand.
And on the lampstand there shall be four cups shaped like nuts.
The knobs and the branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it solid, from a single piece of pure gold.
And you shall make its lamps, seven of them, and set up the lamps, and they shall give light on one side, toward the front.
And you shall make its [?] (tongs?) and the trays that stand beneath it of pure gold.
These vessels shall be made from one talent of pure gold.
See that you make it according to the pattern that I showed you on the mountain.
And you shall make the tabernacle of ten curtains, of [?] fine linen and blue and scarlet and twisted purple. You shall make it with cherubim, cherub by cherub.
The length of one curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, [?] of one curtain; all the curtains shall have one measure.
Five curtains shall be close to one another, one joined to the next, and the five curtains shall be joined, each to its neighbour.
And you shall make loops of blue for it on the [?] (edge) of one curtain, on one side, for joining. And you shall do the same on the second curtain, on the outer side, for joining.
You shall make fifty buttons for it on the one side of the second curtain for fastening, facing each other, so that they line up exactly with one another, each with its counterpart.
And you shall make fifty clasps of gold and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, and it shall be one tabernacle.
And you shall make a covering of hair as a cover over the tabernacle; you shall make eleven covers for it.
The measure of one cover shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of one cover four cubits; the same measure shall be for the elev[en] [?]
…but the half of the shekel as an offering to the Lord.
Everyone who passes into the census, from twenty years old and upward, shall give an offering to the Lord.
The rich shall not add and the poor shall not reduce anything from the half-shekel when giving it as an offering to the Lord and as atonement for your souls.

And you shall take the silver of the offering from the children of Israel and give it for the service of the tent of witness. And it shall be a memorial for the children of Israel before the Lord, as atonement for your souls.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Make a laver of bronze, and its stands of bronze, so that they may wash their hands and their feet; and you shall set it between the tent of witness, and pour water into it.
And Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet
when they go into the tent of witness; they shall wash with water so that they do not die, when they come to the altar to minister and to offer sacrifice.
they shall wash themselves with water, and it shall be a statute for them forever, for them and for their descendants after them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
And you, take fragrant spices: five hundred shekels of choice myrrh, half that weight of fragrant cinnamon, that is, two hundred and fifty, and fragrant cane
and five hundred holy shekels of iris, and one measure of olive oil.
And you shall make it into an anointing oil, a holy ointment made by the perfumer's art; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
And with it you shall anoint the tent of witness and the ark
and all its vessels, and the lampstand and all its vessels, and the altar of incense
and the altar of sacrifices and all its vessels, the table and all its vessels, and the laver and its base.
And you shall consecrate them, and they shall be most holy: whatever touches them shall be made holy.
And you shall anoint Aaron and his sons with it and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
And speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: This shall be a holy anointing oil for you and for your generations.
It shall not be put on a person's body, and you shall not make anything like it with the same mixture, because it is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
Whoever makes anything like it, or puts it on a foreigner, shall be cut off from his people.
And the Lord said to Moses: Take fragrant spices, stacte and onycha and choice galbanum, in equal amounts,
and make them into incense, the work of perfumers, as the makers of ointment make it: blended, pure and holy.
And you shall grind some of it fine and put it before the testimonies in the tent of witness, where I will make myself known to you. The incense shall be most holy to you.
You shall not make incense for yourselves after its recipe: it shall be holy to you, for the Lord.
Whoever makes anything like it in order to smell it shall perish from his people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
See, I have called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, who is of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
And I have filled him with the divine spirit, with wisdom and knowledge and understanding in every kind of work,
to make designs and to be master builder, to work in gold and silver and bronze, and in blue, purple and spun scarlet, and in [?] fine linen,
and in the works of service and in carpentry with wood, to do every kind of work;
and I have given him Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. And I have given knowledge to everyone who is wise of heart. And they shall make everything that I have commanded you:
the tent of witness, and the ark of the covenant, and the mercy seat on it, and the furnishings of the tent,
and the altars, and the table and all its vessels,
the laver and its base,
and the ministering garments of Aaron, and the garments of his sons, for serving me as priests,
and the oil of anointing, and the compounded incense of the sanctuary. They shall do according to all that I have commanded you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take heed and keep my sabbaths, for it is a sign between me and you and your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
And keep my sabbath, for it is holy from the Lord among you. Whoever defiles it shall surely be put to death. Whoever does work on it, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
Six days you shall do your work, but the seventh day is a holy rest of the Lord. Whoever does work on the seventh day shall surely be put to death.
And let the sons of Israel keep the sabbath, observing it throughout their generations as a law
between me and the sons of Israel. It is a sign before me forever, for in six days God made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he rested and [?]
And when he had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the Lord gave Moses the two tablets of testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.

And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, the people gathered around Aaron and said to him: "Arise and make us gods who will go before us, for as for this man Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
And Aaron said to them: "Take off the golden earrings from the ears of your wives and of your daughters"
And all the people took off the golden earrings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
And he took it from their hands and fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a calf by casting molten metal, and he said: "These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt."
And Aaron saw it and built an altar before it, and Aaron sent out a herald to them and said: "Tomorrow is a feast of the Lord."
And they rose early on the next day and offered sacrifices and brought the offering of salvation, and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to sing and play.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him: "Go down quickly from here, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly;
they have quickly turned aside from the way that you commanded them: they have made themselves a calf and have worshiped it and said:
'These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.'
And now let me be, so that I may be enraged with wrath against them and blot them out, and I will make you a great nation."
And Moses implored the Lord God and said: "Why are you enraged with wrath against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a gracious [?] arm?

Lest the Egyptians say: 'With guile the Lord led them out to destroy them on the mountains and to blot them out from the earth.' Cease from the fury of your wrath, and be merciful concerning the wickedness of this your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and spoke to them, saying: 'I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven in number.' And all this land, which you said you would give to their seed, they shall possess forever."
And the Lord had mercy concerning the evil he had said he would do to the people.
And Moses turned and came down from the mountain, with the two tablets of the testimony in his hands, tablets of stone, which were written on both sides, on the one side and on the other.
And the tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
And Joshua the son of Nun heard the noise of the people, and he said to Moses, "I hear a sound of battle in the camp."
And Moses said, "This is not the sound of those who lead in strength, nor the sound of those who lead in victory, but the sound of those who lead in wine that I hear."
And as he came near the camp, he saw the calf and the dances, and Moses became angry with wrath, and he threw the two tablets from his hands and broke them beneath the mountain.
And he took the calf which they had made and burned it with fire and ground it fine, and scattered it on the water and made the children of Israel drink it.
And Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you have brought a great sin upon them?"
And Aaron said to Moses, "Do not be angry, my lord, for you know the impulsiveness of this people."
For they said to me, 'Make us gods who will go before us, for as for Moses, the man who brought us out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
And I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, take it off.' And they gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out."
And when Moses saw the people, that they had run wild, for Aaron had let them run wild, to the gloating of their enemies,
he stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Whoever is on the Lord's side, let him come to me!" And all the sons of Levi came to him.

And he said to them, "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Let each man put his sword on his thigh, and go through and go back and forth from gate to gate through the camp, and let each man kill his brother, and each man his neighbor, and each man the one near to him."
And the sons of Levi did as Moses told them. And on that day three thousand men fell.
And Moses said to them, "Consecrate yourselves today to the Lord with your hands, each man against his son and his brother, so that a blessing may be given to you."
And on the next day Moses said to the people, "You have sinned a great sin, and now I will go up to God, so that he may have mercy on your sins."
Moses returned to the Lord and said, "I beseech you, Lord: the people have sinned a great sin and have made for themselves idols of gold.
And now, if you will forgive their sins, forgive them. But if not, blot me also out of the book in which you have written me."
And the Lord said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned, I will blot him out of my book.
But now go and lead this people to the place of which I told you. Behold, my angel will go before your face. On the day that I visit them, I will bring their sin upon them."
And the Lord struck [?] the people because of the deed of the calf which Aaron had made.

And the Lord said to Moses, "Go, go up from here, you and your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, to the land which I swore to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, saying, 'To your offspring I will give it.'
And I will send my angel before you, and he will drive out the Canaanites and the Amorites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Girgashites and the Jebusites
And may he bring you into the land that flows with milk and honey. But I will not go up with you, for this people is stiff-necked, so that I do not destroy them on the way.
And the people heard this evil word and mourned with mourning.

And the Lord said to the children of Israel: "You are a stiff-necked people. Take care, lest I bring yet another plague upon you and destroy you. And now take off your garments of glory and your ornaments, and I will show you what I will do to you."
And the children of Israel took off their garments and their ornaments at Mount Horeb.
And Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, the tent of witness. And everyone who sought the Lord would go out to the tent outside the camp.
And whenever Moses went to the camp, the people would stand, and each man would look out from the door of his own tent, and they would watch Moses as he went, until he went into the tent.
And when Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the door of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses.
And all the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tent, and all the people would stand, and each man would bow down at the door of his own tent.
And the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, as someone speaks with his own friend, and he would return to the camp. But Moses' servant Joshua, the young man, would not go out of the tent.
And Moses said to the Lord: "See, you tell me to lead this people up, and you do not reveal to me whom you will send with me. Yet you said to me: 'I know you above all, and you have favor with me.'
If I have found favor before you, reveal yourself to me, and let me see you openly, so that I may know that I have found favor before you, and understand that this nation is your people."
And the Lord said: "I myself will go before you and bring you in."
And Moses said to the Lord: "If you do not come with us, do not lead me up from here.

For how will it truly be known that I have found favor before you, I and this your people? Is it not by your coming with us that I and your people will be glorified above all the nations that are on the earth?"
The Lord said to Moses: "This word too that you have spoken I will do, for you have found favor before me, and I know you above all."
And Moses said to the Lord: "Show me your own glory."

And the Lord said to Moses: "I will pass before you in my glory, and I will call out the name of the Lord before you. I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will show favor to whom I will show favor."
And the Lord said to Moses: "You cannot see my face, for there is no one who could see my face and live."
And the Lord said: "Here is a place before you, and you shall stand on the rock.
When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
And I will take away my hand, and then you will see my back, but my face you will not see."

And the Lord said to Moses: "Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
And be ready at dawn, and come up Mount Sinai, and stand there on the summit of the mountain."

And he made the mercy seat on it of pure gold,
and he made the two cherubim of gold:
one cherub at one end of the mercy seat and one cherub at the other end of the mercy seat,
covering the mercy seat with their wings.
And he made the table set before [the Lord] of pure gold,
and he made four rings of gold for it: two rings on one side and two rings on the other side, wide enough so that they could carry it with the poles.
And he made the poles of the ark and of the table and overlaid them with gold.
And he made the utensils of the table: its platters, bowls, ladles and cups, with which offerings are made, all of gold.
And he made the lampstand that gives light, of solid gold:
its shaft and its branches on both of its sides,
its branches growing out of it and projecting, three on one side and three on the other, matching one another.

And their lamp-holders, which stand at their tops, shaped like [?] (serpents?), were made of the same piece, and their sockets were of the same piece, so that the lamps could be placed on them; and the seventh socket was at the tip of the lampstand, on the top, all of solid gold;
and its seven lamps on it were of gold, and its tongs were of gold, and its snuff-dishes were of gold.
This man overlaid the pillars with silver, and he cast gold rings for the pillars, and overlaid the bars with gold, and overlaid the pillars of the veil with gold, and made gold hooks for them.
This man made the gold rings of the tent, the rings of the court, and bronze rings for stretching out the covering of the tent on the upper side.

This man cast the silver capitals of the pillars, and the bronze capitals of the pillars at the door of the tent and at the gates of the court, and he made silver hooks for the pillars. This man overlaid them with silver.
This man made the pegs of the tent and the pegs of the court, all of bronze.
This man made the bronze altar from the bronze censers that had belonged to the men who gathered in revolt with the company of Korah.
This man made all the utensils of the altar: its base, its firepan, its bowls and its flesh-hooks, of bronze.

This man made the surround for the altar, made like a grating, under the firepan, reaching down to its middle. He cast four rings for it at the four corners of the bronze surround of the altar, wide enough for the poles, and with them they carried the altar.
This man made the holy anointing oil and the choice blended incense, prepared by the art of the perfumer.
This man made the bronze laver and its bronze base from the mirrors of the fasting women, who fasted before the doors of the tent of witness, on the day when he set it up.

And he made the laver, so that Moses and Aaron and his sons might wash their hands and their feet in it. Whenever they went into the tent of witness, or whenever they came to the altar to minister, they would wash from it, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
All the gold that was used for the work, for all the work of the holy things, was from the gold of the offering: twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the holy shekel.

And the silver offered by those of the men of the congregation who were counted was a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels; one drachma, half a shekel, for each person, by the holy shekel.
Everyone who went over to be counted, from twenty years old and upward, came to six hundred thousand (sixty myriads) and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
And the ten [?] talents of silver were for casting, by pouring, into the capitals of the tent and the capitals of the veil.
A hundred capitals from the hundred talents: one talent for each capital.
And from the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels they made the hooks for the pillars, and they overlaid the capitals with gold and decorated them.
And the bronze of the offering was four hundred and seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
And from it he made
the bases of the gates of the court, and the pegs of the tent, and the pegs of the court all around the altar.
and all the vessels of the altar, and all the implements of the altar of witness.
And the sons of Israel did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And from the gold that was left over from the offering they made vessels for ministering before the Lord.
And from the blue, scarlet, purple and fine linen that was left over they made garments of ministry for Aaron, so that he might minister in them in the sanctuary.
And they brought the garments to Moses, and the tent and all its vessels, and its clasps, its bases and its pillars,
and the ark of the law and its carrying poles,
and the altar and all its vessels, and the anointing oil, and the blended incense, and the holy lampstand
and its lamps, the lamps for lighting, and the oil for the light,
and the table to be set out before the Lord, and all its vessels for food, and the loaves of the offering,
and the holy garments that are Aaron's, and the priestly garments of his sons,
and the hangings to be spread around the court, with its pillars and bases, and the screen for the door of the tent and for the gate of the court,

and all the vessels of the tent and all its implements, the coverings of rams' skins dyed red, the covering of skins of siavi [?], and the coverings for the other things, and the pegs, and all the implements for the work of the tent of witness:
everything that the Lord had commanded Moses. In this way the sons of Israel made all the preparations.
And Moses saw all the work, and that they had prepared it; it had been made just as the Lord had commanded Moses. And Moses blessed them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
On the first day of the first month, at the beginning of the month, you shall set up the tent of testimony.
And place the ark of testimony, and cover the ark with the veil.
And bring in the table and lay its covering on it, and take the lampstand and set its lamps on it.
And place the golden altar for burning incense before the ark of testimony. And hang the veil of the curtain at the door of the tent of testimony.
And place the altar of offerings in front of the door of the tent of testimony.
And set up the court all around.
And take the anointing oil and anoint the tent and everything that is in it, and consecrate it and all its vessels, and it shall be holy.
And anoint the altar of offerings and all its vessels.
And consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.
And bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tent of testimony and wash them with water.
And clothe Aaron in the holy garments and anoint him, and he shall be holy, to serve me as priest.
And bring his sons and clothe them in garments.
And anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall serve as priests before me.
And Moses did so: as the Lord commanded him, so he did.
And it came to pass in the first month, in the second year after they came out of Egypt, at the beginning of the month, that the tent was set up.
And Moses set up the tent, and set its pillar-capitals in place, and put in its bars, and set up its pillar-capitals.
And he spread out the courts over the tent, and laid the covering of the tent over it on top, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And he took the testimonies and put them into the ark, and put the poles under the ark.
And he brought the ark into the tent, and hung the covering of the curtain, and covered the ark of testimony, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And he placed the table in the tent of testimony on the north side, outside the curtain of the tent of testimony.
And he laid on it the bread of offering before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And he placed the lampstand [?] in the tent of testimony, on the south side.
And he set its lamps on it before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And he placed the golden altar in the tent of testimony in front of the curtain.
And he burned the compounded incense on it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And he set the altar of offerings by the doors of the tent of witness.
And he set up the court around the tent and the altar. And Moses completed all the work.
And the cloud covered the tent of witness, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
And Moses could not enter the tent of witness, because the cloud overshadowed it and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Whenever the cloud rose up from the tent, the sons of Israel would set out to move with their encampments.
If the cloud did not rise, they would not set out to move until the day when the cloud rose,
for the cloud was upon the tent by day, and fire was upon it by night, before all Israel in all their journeyings from camp to camp.
